Samuel Trevor Francis
FRAN-sis
proper noun
From the surname Francis; a nineteenth-century English hymn-writer, author of O the Deep, Deep Love of Jesus.

📖 Biblical Definition

Samuel Trevor Francis was a nineteenth-century English layman, a London merchant and a worker among the poor and the lost, who is remembered for the hymn O the Deep, Deep Love of Jesus. It was written, he tells, in a dark hour when he was tempted to despair, and the love of Christ was set before his soul as a boundless ocean in which he might rest. The dictionary honours Francis for giving the church a hymn that sounds the immeasurable love of Christ, after the prayer of the apostle that the saints might be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height, and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge (Eph 3:18; Eph 3:19). His hymn dwells upon the love that the Lord Himself called the greatest, for greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends (Joh 15:13), the love that is not our love to God but His to us, herein is love, not that we loved God, but that He loved us, and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins (1Jo 4:10). His hymn teaches the troubled and the tempted to rest, as he rested, upon the deep, deep love of Jesus, a love vast as the ocean and free as the wide air, that bears the believer up when all else fails.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A nineteenth-century English hymn-writer, author of O the Deep, Deep Love of Jesus.

SAMUEL TREVOR FRANCIS, a nineteenth-century English layman.

He was a London merchant and a worker among the poor.

He wrote the hymn O the Deep, Deep Love of Jesus.

He wrote it in a dark hour of temptation to despair.

It sounds the immeasurable love of Christ for His people.

📖 Key Scripture

Eph 3:18 — "May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;"

Eph 3:19 — "And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God."

Joh 15:13 — "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends."

1Jo 4:10 — "Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

His hymn sounds the immeasurable love of Christ, teaching the troubled to rest upon a love that passeth knowledge.

expand to see more

What is honourable in Samuel Trevor Francis is the great theme of his hymn, the boundless love of Christ. Tempted to despair, he was given to see that love as an ocean in which his soul might rest, and out of that hour came a hymn that has comforted countless saints. The dictionary honours this hymnody of the love of Christ that passeth knowledge.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the principle to recover is the immeasurable love of Christ, the love the apostle prayed the saints might comprehend in its breadth and length and depth and height. It is not our love to God but His to us, the greatest love, that lays down its life for its friends; herein is love, that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins. Francis teaches the troubled and the tempted to rest upon this deep, deep love of Jesus, vast as the ocean, that bears the believer up when all else fails.
